slot_note: Forecasting lane; seed FC04 (micromobility crew zone) not used. Architecture 3 moves the slot out of the expected-credit-loss world (Bellbird, NSW) into banking stress-testing-capital: a New Zealand regional bank's ICAAP severe-scenario loss on its business book.
niche: a South Island regional bank's ICAAP severe-scenario credit loss on its business lending book, each borrower stressed through the bank's revenue-shock PD table on the fall in its own sales, where a business's sales come from the industries of the firms that pay it, read from the payers named on its operating-account receipts against the NZBN register
answer: NZD 11.5 million: the severe scenario's stressed credit loss on the business banking book in the stress year to 30 September 2027 (Construction 2.5, Manufacturing 1.3, Trade and logistics 2.4, Hospitality, retail and leisure 3.4, Business and property services 1.5, Health, education and personal services 0.4)
analyst_test: A strong analyst who fills the legacy industry codes from the register, reads the standard, the scenario and the PD table correctly and stresses each borrower at its own ANZSIC division's sales path files NZD 10.0 million, about a seventh low, because the receipts show 56 per cent of the book's trading credits come from other divisions, largely the builders and hotels the scenario hits hardest.
domain_test: The deciding quantity is each business borrower's stressed PD under the ICAAP severe scenario, set by the fall in its own sales through the bank's revenue-shock PD table, with stressed LGD and EAD summed over the book; with another field's nouns the scenario's industry sales paths, the PD table, the stressed LGDs and the operating-account receipts have nothing to attach to, and how a sector shock reaches a lender's borrowers through who pays them is credit stress transmission.
layer1: an operating-account credits extract whose payer names the clearing system upper-cased and cut at 20 characters, with merchant-acquirer settlement batches, branch cash, own-account transfers, GST refunds, insurance claims, loan advances and credit interest among the trading credits
an NZBN register extract with legal and trading names and BIC codes, payers sending a trading name for some firms
a business lending book whose industry field is blank or on the legacy 1993 code set for borrowers migrated from the earlier lending platform, customer names as Ltd or Limited
a collections receipts workbook carrying the collection agency's statement upload beside its remittances, guarantors' receipts on their own personal cases
a default register recording a connected group's cross-default under the group lead's customer number, customer numbers merged in a March 2026 clean-up, grade overrides kept in a separate log
stakeholder_role: head of capital management at a regional bank, preparing the ICAAP's business-book stress for the board

spine.entity: one credit to a business borrower's operating account

world.geography: New Zealand, Canterbury, Otago and Southland
world.org_type: regional bank with a business lending book

driver: A unit's loss under a shock that hits groups of others unevenly is set by the share of its income each group pays it, read from who pays it, and it responds to its own income loss along a steep curve, so mapping each unit to the shock its own label names leaves units paid by the hardest-hit groups at a mild rate, overstates units of a hard-hit label paid by sheltered groups, and files the total low.
driver_concrete: Orari Bank stresses each business borrower through its revenue-shock PD table on the fall in its own sales, and a borrower's sales are what its customers pay it: the payers named on its operating-account receipts, matched to the NZBN register, give each borrower's sales by paying industry, and the scenario's industry sales paths applied to those shares give its fall; stressing every borrower at its own ANZSIC division's path leaves the transport, wholesale, admin and professional firms paid by builders and hotels at a mild multiplier and files the year's loss low.
stump: A strong solver stresses each business borrower at the scenario's sales path for its own ANZSIC division, applies the revenue-shock PD table, the stressed LGDs and EAD, and files NZD 10.0 million; the step that lands it there is reading each borrower's sales fall off its own industry when its receipts show who pays it, and the builders, hotels and tour operators that pay much of the book cut their spending by a quarter.

differentiation.task146: task146 releases a seasonal pool built by refused first attempts when a calendar period turns; here nothing is pooled or released: each borrower's scenario sales fall is the paying industries' falls weighted by its receipts.
differentiation.task165: task165 conditions an upgrade's gain on how much of a unit the old service level left untreated; here no treatment or gain is measured: a filed scenario shock reaches each borrower through the industries of the firms that pay it.
differentiation.task173: task173's lineage conditions a comeback rate on the opener's group and tenure on a service desk; here the conditioning is each borrower's own mix of paying industries read from its receipts, applied to a filed sector scenario, with no rate carried from a history mix.
differentiation.task465: task465 counts units carrying two traits no large source records together; here every borrower's paying industries are recorded, and the step is to read the scenario's shock through them rather than through the borrower's own code.
differentiation.task54: task54 multiplies an exposure integral under a re-sequenced plan with a rule recovered from closed cases; here no rule is recovered and nothing is re-sequenced.
differentiation.task156: task156 v2 scales a station's infiltration with sewer length below a water table; here a lender's borrower is stressed on its own sales fall read through who pays it.
differentiation.task133: Architecture 3 leaves the slot's personal-loan ECL world and its survival and truncation drivers entirely: a business-book stress test where the step is how a sector scenario reaches each borrower.
differentiation.task134: task134 v3 prices a raised zoning allowance by each lot's chance of being rebuilt once the best permitted option out-pays what stands there; here no option is chosen and nothing is rebuilt: a filed sector scenario reaches each business borrower through the industries of the firms that pay it, read from its receipts, and its stressed PD follows its own sales fall.
differentiation.task131: task131 moves a randomised tariff's load out of a peak window and finds the surge that returns when the window closes, judged on a summed demand curve's maximum; here nothing is randomised, shifted in time or summed to a peak: a filed sector scenario reaches each business borrower through the industries of the firms that pay it, read from its receipts, and its stressed PD follows its own sales fall.

lineage.fate: hardening loop 1: survival to date landed on the portal (one model stumped, the other filed AUD 13,773,000 and scored 100 per cent, banking every inheriting ask: stage by product, drawdown year, stage 3 count)
lineage.driver: A cumulative outcome curve is filed from each unit's entry, and every unit in scope has already survived part of it, so its forward probability is the curve's remaining increments divided by its own survival to date; reading the curve from entry for every unit overstates the total, and shifting it to the unit's age without the division understates it.
lineage.stump: A competent solver applies the cumulative PD curve to each loan's remaining months counted from the reporting date as if it were a term structure and books an allowance about 43 per cent high; the step that lands it there is reading a curve indexed by months on book as if every performing loan were new.

lineage.fate: round 2 (2026-10-14): never judged on the portal; the 10/10 audit found it compliant but weak: a rung added above the step the v1 portal winner solved, with the development sample's outcome column beside a 'share of every loan drawn' header signposting it
lineage.driver: A cumulative outcome curve is filed as shares of every unit that ever entered, so units that left by a competing exit stay in its base; a unit still in scope at its age has come through both the outcome and the competing exit, so its forward probability is the curve's increment divided by the share of entrants still present and outcome-free at that age, which only the unit-level development record gives; dividing by one less the curve to date leaves the exited units in the base and understates the total, and a hazard rolled forward with no competing exit overstates it.
lineage.stump: A competent solver reads the PD curve as cumulative default by months on book, divides each loan's forward increments by its survival to date, 1 - C(a), and books about AUD 11.74 million against AUD 13,160,000, 10.8 per cent low; the step that lands it there is taking the curve's shares as shares of loans still open when they are shares of every loan drawn, so the loans repaid in full by month a stay in the at-risk base.

lineage.architecture: v2 (round 2, left truncation in the loan record)
lineage.fate: landed on the portal (the survival-to-date conditioning was the field's reflex); re-rooted 2026-11-01 at the Batch 3 queue reset (one architecture per world: the Bellbird personal-loan ECL world is closed)
lineage.driver: A unit-level record that took over an earlier record's units holds them only if they were still present at the takeover, so the months they spent before it are months the record never watched, not months they were seen to come through; outcome rates by age must count each taken-over unit only from its age at the takeover, and counting it from its own start fills every early age's denominator with exposure that could not end in the outcome, so the rates and the forward total for a young population come out low.
lineage.stump: A strong solver builds each product's monthly default and repayment rates by month on book from the loan record, counting every loan from its drawdown, rolls each performing loan forward from its own month on book, and books AUD 11.6 million against AUD 13.2 million (12.3 per cent low); the step that lands it there is counting the 16,479 loans the record took over at the October 2019 go-live as at risk from their drawdown, when the record holds them only because they were still open that day.

notes: Strategy other: exposure transmission through counterparties. Each borrower's scenario shock is the shock of the industries that pay it, weighted by its receipts, an input-output reading of a filed sector scenario; no rate is measured on one mix and carried to another (so not composition_mix), and no outcome is split between causes (so not decomposition_attribution).
